findings.evidence: scripts/bump_manifest_fixtures/mathlib_first/root.json pins plausible fb13df72, aesop a90fbf7b, batteries 33131f4f (= mathlib_first/TauCeti.json); scripts/bump_manifest_fixtures/three_deps/Physlib.json pins plausible 118aa17e, aesop 355695d5, batteries f2effa3d (= three_deps/mathlib.json). Both manifests also list the direct deps in reverse lakefile order with the winner first (root.json: TauCeti, Physlib, mathlib; base.json: mathlib, TauCeti, Physlib), consistent with last-require-wins. The case is unreachable today only because three_deps/TauCeti.json pins no package outside mathlib's set.
findings.fix: Have step 1b emit the full ordered require list (the awk already walks it) and have `problems` pick, among the owners of a package, the one declared last in the lakefile — TauCeti over Physlib today — instead of `candidates = ml_entry or [q for _, q in owners[n]]` accepting any. If the relaxation is kept deliberately, drop the "no real manifest shows which Lake takes" justification in all three places and state it as a deliberate widening.
findings.issue: "when two do, either is accepted, because no real manifest shows which of them Lake takes" is false on the PR's own evidence. In mathlib_first/root.json (requires: mathlib, Physlib, TauCeti) the eight disputed packages are TauCeti's — and Physlib pins them identically to mathlib (plausible 118aa17e / aesop 355695d5 / batteries f2effa3d in three_deps/Physlib.json vs fb13df72 / a90fbf7b / 33131f4f in root.json). So Lake took the later-declared TauCeti's entry over the earlier-declared Physlib's: the same last-require-wins rule the guard now enforces (check-bump.sh:99-112) also determines the Physlib-vs-TauCeti case, and the current lakefile declares TauCeti after Physlib. Accepting either is therefore an unjustified widening: the guard can pass a manifest no `lake update` would write, in the one place where its "everything else is derived" claim is supposed to be deterministic. Same false claim in docs/dependency-bumps.md:109-110 and scripts/bump_manifest_fixtures/mathlib_first/README.md:15-16.

summary: The lakefile premise and the v4-tag narrowing from the previous round are fixed and now machine-checked. One claim is still wrong: the justification for accepting either entry when Physlib and TauCeti both pin a package is contradicted by the PR's own mathlib_first fixture, which settles that case under the same last-require-wins rule the guard enforces.
